10.0.0.en: And Rehoboam went to Shechem: for to Shechem were all Israel come to make him king. [1]

10.0.1.en: Rehoboam is the only son of Solomon whom history records, and he was born to Solomon of Naamah the Ammonitess (1 Kgs 14:31), who may have been the daughter of Hanun, king of Ammon.

10.0.2.en: “Rehoboam” means “the enlargement of the people,” and he was so called in remembrance of the completion of the acquisition of the Promised Land, which was not possessed fully until the last days of David (Ex 34:24). It is said of him that because of his lack of wisdom the kingdom was divided.

10.0.3.en: Some see that Solomon spoke of himself when he said: [He that begetteth a fool doeth it to his sorrow: and the father of a fool hath no joy] (Prov 17:21). For his soul became embittered in his last days when he realized that he would leave his kingdom to a son who lacked understanding. He expressed this by saying: [Yea, I hated all my labour which I had taken under the sun: because I should leave it unto the man that shall be after me. And who knoweth whether he shall be a wise man or a fool? yet shall he have rule over all my labour wherein I have laboured, and wherein I have shewed myself wise under the sun. This is also vanity... For there is a man whose labour is in wisdom, and in knowledge, and in equity; yet to a man that hath not laboured therein shall he leave it for his portion. This also is vanity and a great evil] (Eccl 2:18-19, 21).

10.1.0.en: The wise man does not know what his heirs will do with what he labored for and acquired, but the one who is bound to heavenly wisdom in his life and conduct leaves them an inheritance of blessing that is not lost. What did the priest Zacharias and Elizabeth bequeath to St. John the Baptist? Their constant holy prayers and their righteousness in the Lord. Their life was a support to him in the wilderness while he was deprived of their visible care! 1. With Solomon's wisdom and his capabilities and sincere intention, he turned aside by his marriage to idolatrous women, and part of the fruit of this was that his son did not walk in the mind of his father. 2. Solomon erred in his excess in building projects and in spending on his wives, so he burdened his people with taxes, and this was a basic factor in the division of the kingdom. 3. Some see in these murmurers that they forgot what Solomon had done, for the kingdom lived forty years in peace and prosperity without wars, and his age was marked by prosperity for all. 4. Here the fault is shared: the people murmured and forgot the blessings of Solomon's age, and on the other hand Rehoboam put on his father's crown but did not enjoy his mind and wisdom. Nor did he enjoy the spirit of sincere shepherding that his grandfather David had. Rehoboam did not heed the wisdom of Job and his humility, for he said that he did not despise the cause of his manservant or of his maidservant when they contended with him (Job 31:13). The people needed gentle words from Rehoboam, and then they would be his servants for ever with all gladness [7]. For kind words cost us only a little self-denial, and by them we gain countless blessings.

10.1.1.en: Shechem All Israel gathered at Shechem to make Rehoboam the son of Solomon king over them.

10.1.2.en: Shechem lies about 40 miles north of Jerusalem, and it is a fitting center for such an important gathering, for it lies in the territory of Manasseh, and this pleased the people who lived in the north. In Shechem is the tomb of Joseph (Josh 24:32). Abraham, the father of all the Jews, was in Shechem (Gen 12:6), and also Jacob (Gen 33:18). And Joshua with all the tribes of Israel renewed the covenant with God in Shechem (Josh 24).

10.1.3.en: So the choice of Shechem carried the possibility of planting the spirit of unity between the north and the south, but sadly Rehoboam's conduct caused a grave schism and the division of the kingdom.

10.1.4.en: It was good that the gathering took place in Shechem, but sadly we do not hear of a renewal of the covenant with God, as happened when Saul became king, and also David (2 Sam 2:4) and Solomon (1 Kgs 1:28-30).

10.1.5.en: If we may say so, when Rehoboam received the kingdom God was not first in his heart, and he did not feel that he had received this work from His hands.

10.2.0.en: 2 And it came to pass, when Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who was in Egypt, whither he had fled from the presence of Solomon the king, heard it, that Jeroboam returned out of Egypt. 3 And they sent and called him. So Jeroboam and all Israel came and spake to Rehoboam, saying, 4 “Thy father made our yoke grievous: now therefore ease thou somewhat the grievous servitude of thy father, and his heavy yoke that he put upon us, and we will serve thee.” 5 And he said unto them, “Come again unto me after three days.” And the people departed. 6 And king Rehoboam took counsel with the old men that had stood before Solomon his father while he yet lived, saying, “What counsel give ye me to return answer to this people?” 7 And they spake unto him, saying, “If thou be kind to this people, and please them, and speak good words to them, they will be thy servants for ever.” 8 But he forsook the counsel which the old men gave him, and took counsel with the young men that were brought up with him, that stood before him. 9 And he said unto them, “What advice give ye that we may return answer to this people, which have spoken to me, saying, Ease somewhat the yoke that thy father did put upon us?” 10 And the young men that were brought up with him spake unto him, saying, “Thus shalt thou answer the people that spake unto thee, saying, Thy father made our yoke heavy, but make thou it somewhat lighter for us; thus shalt thou say unto them, My little finger shall be thicker than my father's loins. 11 For whereas my father put a heavy yoke upon you, I will put more to your yoke: my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.” 12 So Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam on the third day, as the king bade, saying, “Come again to me on the third day.” 13 And the king answered them roughly; and king Rehoboam forsook the counsel of the old men, 14 And answered them after the advice of the young men, saying, “My father made your yoke heavy, but I will add thereto: my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.” 15 So the king hearkened not unto the people: for the cause was of God, that the LORD might perform his word, which he spake by the hand of Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam the son of Nebat.

10.2.1.en: And it came to pass, when Jeroboam the son of Nebat heard it, (who was in Egypt, whither he had fled from the presence of Solomon the king)

10.2.2.en: That Jeroboam returned out of Egypt. [2]

10.3.0.en: And they sent and called him. So Jeroboam and all Israel came and spake to Rehoboam, saying, [3]

10.4.0.en: Thy father made our yoke grievous: now therefore ease thou somewhat the grievous servitude of thy father, and his heavy yoke that he put upon us, and we will serve thee. [4]

10.4.1.en: The people were groaning under the heavy yoke of Solomon, for he did not bear the spirit of his father David, who truly loved his people and gave himself for their service.

10.4.2.en: As for Solomon, he did not serve his people; what occupied him was the fulfillment of his projects and his desires, in which he went to excess. As for Rehoboam, listening to the groaning of the people did not concern him. Rehoboam did not understand the meaning of leadership, for he was not a good shepherd like his grandfather David.

10.4.3.en: Solomon divided the state, with regard to the responsibilities of work, into twelve districts (1 Kgs 4:7-19), and it seems that he excepted the tribe of Judah; it followed from this that when he conscripted officials for the work he exempted Judah from the work (1 Kgs 5:13-18). This is what the prophet Samuel had indicated beforehand when the people asked for a king to be set over them like all the nations. He warned them, saying: “This will be the manner of the king that shall reign over you: He will take your sons, and appoint them for himself, for his chariots, and to be his horsemen... And he will appoint him captains over thousands, and captains over fifties; and will set them to ear his ground, and to reap his harvest... and ye shall be his servants” (1 Sam 8:11-18).

10.4.4.en: v There are indeed many other things able to give us boldness before God, and to show us radiant and approved, but most of all that which brings a good will from above is tender care for our neighbor, which Christ required of Peter[1].

10.4.5.en: St. John Chrysostom v We read of cases that are not unique, even with regard to kings, of how effective kindness (“love”) is, and how harmful are pride and rebellious words, since they led to the shaking and destruction of kingdoms.

10.4.6.en: v How many murmurings did the people direct against Moses, and yet he bore them! And when the Lord wanted to take vengeance for him on them, he preferred to offer himself to death in order to save them from the divine wrath (Ex 32:32).

10.4.7.en: With what tenderness Moses spoke with the people, even after they had sinned against him! He comforted them by his works, and consoled and encouraged them by his prophecy of the future.

10.4.8.en: Although he spoke with God much, yet when he spoke with the people he spoke gently and with joy.

10.4.9.en: v Moses was qualified to become above all men, so that they could not look upon his face (Ex 34:30). And he captivated them, so that they loved him because of his tenderness more than their admiration for the miracles that were done by his hands.

10.4.10.en: v David also followed in the steps of Moses, for when he was chosen to rule the people, he was gentle and compassionate, contrite in spirit, persevering, ready to show affection.

10.4.11.en: For before he sat on the throne he offered himself to destruction for all (1 Sam 17:22), and when he became king he made himself equal to all in war, sharing the work with them.

10.4.12.en: He was encouraging in battles, gentle in judgment (among the people), patient in bearing insults, more ready to bear with others than to return wrong for wrong. Therefore he was dear to all...

10.4.13.en: He loved the brave, even those who were his enemies, thinking that justice requires honoring those who endured much in war, as if they were men of his own army.

10.4.14.en: He admired Abner, the brave commander, although he was one of his adversaries; therefore he did not despise him when he asked him for peace but honored him, making a special feast for him (1 Kgs 2:5). And when he was killed by treachery, David grieved for him and lamented him...

10.4.15.en: It is no small thing for a king to show humility in his deeds, counting himself as the least of his people, refusing to eat or drink water that others had risked their lives to bring.

10.4.16.en: This David asked that God pour out His wrath upon him instead of its being poured out upon the people, offering himself to the destroying angel, saying: “Lo, I have sinned, and I have done wickedly: but these sheep, what have they done? let thine hand, I pray thee, be against me, and against my father's house” (2 Sam 24:17).

10.4.17.en: St. Ambrose v The good shepherd imitates the Chief Shepherd of shepherds, who said: Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends, so that he loves his neighbor more than himself.

10.4.18.en: The shepherd in name does not love his neighbor as himself, so he neglects him until the thief takes him or the wolf snatches him.

10.5.0.en: And he said unto them, Come again unto me after three days. And the people departed. [5]

10.5.1.en: It was good that Rehoboam gave himself time to answer without haste, and good that he consulted the wise elders, but he erred because he did not seek the counsel of the Lord, and did not lift his heart to Him in prayer and the offering of sacrifices.

10.6.0.en: And king Rehoboam took counsel with the old men that had stood before Solomon his father while he yet lived, saying, What counsel give ye me to return answer to this people? [6]

10.7.0.en: And they spake unto him, saying, If thou be kind to this people, and please them, and speak good words to them, they will be thy servants for ever. [7]

10.7.1.en: The elders knew very well that the people were not rebelling against the king; they were ready to serve him with a good heart, if he were good and bore in his heart the spirit of sincere shepherding.

10.7.2.en: What occupied the heart of good leaders was that they were serving God Himself by their service and their self-giving for their people. They counted themselves servants, not men of authority.

10.7.3.en: The Word of God Himself came incarnate, not to be served but to serve and to give His life a ransom for many (Lk 22:24-27; Phil 2:1-13). He trained His disciples in leadership through service and the washing of the feet of those served (Jn 13:1-17), and He asked of us: “Whosoever will be great among you, let him be your minister; And whosoever will be chief among you, let him be your servant” (Mt 20:26-27).

10.7.4.en: v May he who is a ruler not be puffed up because of his work, lest he fall from the blessedness of humility, but it is fitting for him to know true humility as a service to many... May the greatest be as the least.

10.7.5.en: v It is fitting for those who occupy the chief positions to be ready to offer even bodily service, after the example of the Lord who washed the feet of His disciples. Therefore it was said, “(Let) the leader (be) as the servant[2]”.

10.7.6.en: St. Basil the Great v Keep faith and humility within yourself, for by them you find mercy and help, and hear divine words in your heart, and your guardian angel accompanies you outwardly and in secret.

10.7.7.en: v Humility is the garment of Godhead, for the incarnate Word clothed Himself with it, and spoke to us of it through our bodies. So everyone who puts it on truly imitates Him who came down from His height, and covered the virtue of His greatness with humility, and veiled His glory with it lest creation be burned by the sight of it.

10.7.8.en: v No one hates the humble, nor rebukes him, nor despises him, for his Master loves him. He loves everyone, and everyone loves him and longs for him everywhere, and wherever he is found they look at him as a luminous angel, and give him honor.

10.7.9.en: v Humility is a hidden power which the perfect saints obtain after the completion of their course, and grace gives this power only to those who are perfect in virtue[3].

10.8.0.en: But he forsook the counsel which the old men gave him, and took counsel with the young men that were brought up with him, that stood before him [8]

10.8.1.en: His forsaking the counsel of the elders and consulting the young men was not in order to learn of another counsel and compare the two counsels, but he rejected the counsel of the elders because it was not according to his desire. For he did not want to serve, but to rule.

10.8.2.en: It is fitting for the servant to listen to the elders as to the young, looking at the whole community, with its elders and children and youths and women, as one family interacting together in the spirit of love and unity in humility before the Lord.

10.8.3.en: The Fathers of the Church speak to us of the need of the young for the elders, as of the elders for the young. The Apostle says: “Yea, all of you be subject one to another, and be clothed with humility: for God resisteth the proud, and giveth grace to the humble” (1 Pet 5:5).

10.8.4.en: The young Elisha began to work with the elder Elijah. St. Ambrose admires the joint work between the elder and the young servants, for each has a role that completes the other's.

10.8.5.en: v How beautiful is the unity between the elder and the young.

10.8.6.en: One bears witness, and the other gives rest.

10.8.7.en: One leads, and the other gives joy...

10.8.8.en: What of Elijah and Elisha? Although the Holy Bible did not say much about Elisha's being young, yet we can understand that he was the younger.

10.8.9.en: In the Acts of the Apostles, Barnabas took Mark with him, and Paul took Silas (Acts 15:39-40) and Timothy (Acts 16:3) and Titus (Titus 1:5).

10.8.10.en: We see also a division of duties among them. The elders lead, offering counsel, and the young show vitality of work. Most likely they were all alike in virtue, but not in years. They rejoice in their unity, as Peter and John did.

10.8.11.en: We read in the Gospel that John was young, by the testimony of his own words, and yet he was not inferior to the elders in merits and wisdom. He bears mature and dignified traits and prudence in his mind[4].

10.9.0.en: And he said unto them (and asked them), What advice give ye that we may return answer to this people, which have spoken to me, saying,

10.9.1.en: Ease somewhat the yoke that thy father did put upon us? [9]

10.10.0.en: And the young men that were brought up with him spake unto him, saying,

10.10.1.en: Thus shalt thou answer the people that spake unto thee, saying, Thy father made our yoke heavy, but make thou it somewhat lighter for us; thus shalt thou say unto them,

10.10.2.en: My little finger shall be thicker than my father's loins. [10]

10.10.3.en: Rehoboam did not heed the words of his father, wise in the Lord: “A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger. The tongue of the wise useth knowledge aright: but the mouth of fools poureth out foolishness” (Prov 15:1-2). Rehoboam did not realize the gravity of the tongue, for it is said: “There is that speaketh like the piercings of a sword: but the tongue of the wise is health” (Prov 12:18).

10.11.0.en: For whereas my father put a heavy yoke upon you, I will put more to your yoke:

10.11.1.en: my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions. [11]

10.11.2.en: His words came violent and his tone harsh, so that instead of easing the yoke that his father had put on the people, even with a gentle word, he assured them that he would make it heavier, until he made it unbearable. He thought that by this he was exercising his right as a king with authority, indifferent to the welfare of the people and their feelings. He took a grave decision that shatters the unity of the kingdom, and shatters the personality of Rehoboam himself!

10.11.3.en: What David the righteous king had built, his grandson Rehoboam, in David's third generation, destroys.

10.11.4.en: Rehoboam erred in that he did not consult God, for he had no personal relationship with Him.

10.11.5.en: Scorpions: these are whips whose ends terminate in a pointed iron material, and their stroke resembles the sting of scorpions.

10.12.0.en: So Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam on the third day, as the king bade, saying,

10.12.1.en: Come again to me on the third day. [12]

10.13.0.en: And the king answered them roughly; and king Rehoboam forsook the counsel of the old men [13]

10.13.1.en: It is fitting for the leader not to meet the agitation of his subordinates with violence, lest he add oil to the fire, but rather to hold the wheel of leadership calmly and steadily through the storm until it passes in safety.

10.14.0.en: And answered them after the advice of the young men, saying,

10.14.1.en: My father made your yoke heavy, but I will add thereto:

10.14.2.en: my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions. [14]

10.15.0.en: So the king hearkened not unto the people: for the cause was of God, that the LORD might perform his word, which he spake by the hand of Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam the son of Nebat. [15]

10.15.1.en: If God, the Almighty, had declared beforehand through Ahijah the Shilonite what would happen [15], this does not justify Rehoboam's folly, nor lessen his responsibility for acting with arrogance and haughtiness, which the Lord used to carry out His purposes.

10.15.2.en: Often God permits the evil of fathers to be visited upon their children, if they walk in the same way as their fathers. Solomon left the Lord, so God permitted most of the people to leave Rehoboam the son of Solomon. God permits this to urge fathers who do not care about the troubles that come upon them to realize that what they do will return upon their children more than they imagine, for many are concerned that no harm should befall their children.

10.15.3.en: If God permitted the carrying out of His threats, so that the sin of Solomon was visited upon his son Rehoboam, at the same time He did not forget His promise to David, and therefore He kept two tribes for his grandson Rehoboam.

10.15.4.en: The Psalmist says in the Lord's words: “If they break my statutes, and keep not my commandments; Then will I visit their transgression with the rod, and their iniquity with stripes. Nevertheless my lovingkindness will I not utterly take from him, nor suffer my faithfulness to fail. My covenant will I not break, nor alter the thing that is gone out of my lips” (Ps 89:31-34).

10.16.0.en: 16 And when all Israel saw that the king would not hearken unto them, the people answered the king, saying, “What portion have we in David? and we have none inheritance in the son of Jesse: every man to your tents, O Israel: and now, David, see to thine own house.” So all Israel went to their tents. 17 But as for the children of Israel that dwelt in the cities of Judah, Rehoboam reigned over them. 18 Then king Rehoboam sent Hadoram that was over the tribute; and the children of Israel stoned him with stones, that he died. But king Rehoboam made speed to get him up to his chariot, to flee to Jerusalem. 19 And Israel rebelled against the house of David unto this day.

10.16.1.en: And when all Israel saw that the king would not hearken unto them, the people answered the king, saying,

10.16.2.en: What portion have we in David!

10.16.3.en: And we have none inheritance in the son of Jesse!

10.16.4.en: Every man to your tents, O Israel.

10.16.5.en: And now, David, see to thine own house!

10.16.6.en: So all Israel went to their tents. [16]

10.16.7.en: Although it was Rehoboam who hardened his heart and acted without wisdom, the ten tribes counted their rebellion as not against Rehoboam but against David: “What portion have we in David? and we have none inheritance in the son of Jesse!” [16] And God counted this rejection as a rejection of His grace and His promises. So Judah became in God's eyes the representative of His people, and Israel was cut off from it.

10.16.8.en: Their evil appears from the following: 1. The great majority of the ten tribes accepted the worship of the calves. 2. They expelled the priests and the Levites, and appointed priests for the idols. 3. Those faithful to the faith went to Jerusalem and the cities of Judah.

10.17.0.en: But as for the children of Israel that dwelt in the cities of Judah, Rehoboam reigned over them. [17]

10.18.0.en: Then king Rehoboam sent Hadoram that was over the tribute; and the children of Israel stoned him with stones, that he died.

10.18.1.en: But king Rehoboam made speed to get him up to his chariot, to flee to Jerusalem [18]

10.18.2.en: Just as Rehoboam took the wrong counsel, so when he wanted to remedy his error he chose the wrong mediator. He chose Hadoram who was over the tribute, in whom they saw a representative of the heavy yoke that Solomon had put upon them. He did not send a man known for wisdom and gentleness whom they could listen to, but sent one whom they could not bear to see because of his position as general overseer of the forced labor.

10.19.0.en: And Israel rebelled against the house of David unto this day. [19]

10.19.1.en: Take, O Lord, the wheel of leadership!

10.19.2.en: v In great Shechem Rehoboam met all Israel.

10.19.3.en: He received the throne of his father, marked by glory and riches.

10.19.4.en: He thought in himself that as a king he commands and is obeyed.

10.19.5.en: He did not hand the wheel of leadership over to You, nor did he renew the covenant with You and with Your people!

10.19.6.en: v He thought that all the people were slaves to him.

10.19.7.en: He did not imitate You, O King of kings, the Good Shepherd!

10.19.8.en: He did not imitate his grandfather David in the purity of his heart.

10.19.9.en: Nor did he hide himself in You, that You might work in him and through him!

10.19.10.en: v The people longed to see him truly as a grandson of David.

10.19.11.en: They asked him to lift from them the weight of the yoke that his father Solomon had put upon them.

10.19.12.en: They did not refuse to serve him, but asked him to be gentle with them, and then they would serve him faithfully.

10.19.13.en: v Rehoboam did not know to ask the Lord for counsel.

10.19.14.en: God was not the leader of his thought and his life.

10.19.15.en: He consulted the elders as well as the young.

10.19.16.en: He accepted the counsel that agreed with his desire.

10.19.17.en: In pride together with folly, violence found a place in his heart as in his mind.

10.19.18.en: v Grant me, O Lord, that You take the wheel of leadership.

10.19.19.en: Then I will walk by Your Spirit, O You who are all love and tenderness.

10.19.20.en: I long to be poured out for the sake of Your people.

10.19.21.en: And to find delight in serving all.

10.19.22.en: v Remove from my heart all harshness, and from my mouth every wounding word, that I may truly be Your ambassador!

10.19.23.en: v By violence the people lost their unity.

10.19.24.en: And schism and discord entered among them.

10.19.25.en: Grant me love and tenderness, that all may gather together to You.

10.19.26.en: Be the Leader of Your people, that in the spirit of unity all may go from strength to strength.

10.19.27.en: And all may experience true glory.

10.19.28.en: And all may walk in a delightful journey in Your company.

10.19.29.en: And all may set out as though to Your heavens!

10.19.30.en: To You be glory, O Leader, the Good Shepherd!
